rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for something, someone, or weather that is very hot.

example.english: It’s really boiling today; I’m covered in sweat after being outside for just a little while.
example.traditional: 今日真係好熱，我出街一陣已經成身汗。
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 zan1 hai6 hou2 jit6 ngo5 ceot1 gaai1 jat1 zan6 ji5 ging1 seng4 san1 hon6

rows.note: Use this as an exaggerated colloquial complaint when the speaker feels unbearably hot.

example.english: It’s boiling today; I’m sweating all over after walking just a couple of steps.
example.traditional: 今日熱到痴線，我行兩步都成身汗。
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 jit6 dou3 ci1 sin3 ngo5 haang4 loeng5 bou6 dou1 seng4 san1 hon6

rows.note: Use this for a liquid or object that is at boiling or piping-hot temperature.

example.english: The soup is still boiling, so be careful not to scald yourself.
example.traditional: 啲湯仲滾熱㗎，小心唔好辣親。
example.jyutping: di1 tong1 zung6 gwan2 jit6 gaa3 siu2 sam1 m4 hou2 laat6 can1

rows.note: Choose this for vivid, scorching physical heat, especially from an object or the weather.

example.english: The stone is boiling hot from the sun; even sitting on it is unbearable.
example.traditional: 塊石頭曬到熱辣辣，坐低都頂唔順。
example.jyutping: faai3 sek6 tau4 saai3 dou3 jit6 laat6 laat6 co5 dai1 dou1 ding2 m4 seon6
